name: Lough Neagh

attributes.attribute: large lake in the northern province of Ulster
began as a well whose overflowing waters formed the lake
drowned and became a mermaid at Lough Neagh

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lough Neagh is a large lake in the northern province of Ulster, Ireland. The lake began as a well. When a careless woman left the lid off, the waters rushed out and spread to form the lake. The flood drowned the family of the maiden Li Ban, who was left alone beneath the waves with her small lapdog. Watching the fish play, Li Ban prayed to become one herself. She was turned into a mermaid with a salmon's tail, and her dog became an otter. Other tales from the region say a magical city appears beneath the lake's waters on clear days.

okr.objective: Document the origin legend of Lough Neagh and the transformation of the maiden Li Ban.
key_results: The lake formed when an uncovered well overflowed
